cover.headline: Food delivery plus cash is about what the market pays; Instamart is the swing factor
cover.lead: Swiggy runs India's #2 food-delivery app and the #3 quick-commerce network (Instamart). At ₹{{P.last|num}} the stock is 46% below its October-2025 high. Q1FY27 showed progress: food delivery earned ₹292 cr (3.1% of order value) and Instamart's contribution margin reached breakeven in May. But Instamart still lost ₹778 cr in the quarter while Blinkit, its larger rival, made a profit, and in September MSCI dropped the stock as foreign ownership hit the new 49.5% cap. Our view: food delivery and ~₹14,367 cr of cash are worth roughly the whole market value, so the market gives Instamart little. Our sum of the parts gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**, just short of our BUY line: **we initiate with HOLD (high risk).** Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}} ({{scen.bear.upside|chg}}).

arguments.h: Food delivery is profitable and improving, but losing share
arguments.p: Adjusted EBITDA was ₹292 cr in Q1FY27, 3.1% of order value (GOV), up from 0.9% two years ago. Order value grew 17.4%. But Zomato grew faster (net order value +20.1%) and earns 5.6%. Swiggy is a solid #2 that is not closing the gap.

arguments.h: Instamart: margins turning, losses still deep
arguments.p: Instamart lost ₹778 cr in Q1FY27 (−9.8% of GOV); Blinkit made ₹102 cr. Blinkit has 2,443 dark stores to Instamart's 1,171 and grew net order value 86% to Instamart's 39%. Management reached contribution breakeven in May, but says EBITDA breakeven needs ~2.5x today's scale and gives no date.

arguments.h: The cash buys time, not victory
arguments.p: Cash and investments were ₹14,367 cr at June 2026, with no debt other than leases; Q1 burn was ~₹700 cr. The CFO expects to break even on cash over the next two quarters (food profits and interest covering Instamart). Swiggy will not need new money soon, but every year of losses uses up value that shareholders already own.

arguments.h: The market gives Instamart little; so do we
arguments.p: At ₹{{P.last|num}}, market value (~₹69,031 cr) less cash leaves ~₹54,664 cr for all the businesses: about 29x our FY28E food EBITDA, with nothing left for Instamart. We value food at 30x and Instamart at a small positive (0.2x order value less the losses still to fund), so our target sits {{dcf.upside|chg}} above the price. The street's median target is ₹360.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (late Oct-2026): does Instamart's order value re-accelerate (management hopes for double-digit growth on the quarter) while contribution stays within 0 to −1%?
Instamart moves to an inventory (1P) model within 2-4 quarters of the Aug-2026 approval: watch contribution margin and working capital.
Food delivery growth against Zomato: does the gap narrow?
Forced selling: MSCI and NSE index deletions (Sep-2026) as foreign ownership sits at the 49.5% cap.

sections.title: One app, five businesses: how Swiggy makes money

blocks.p: Swiggy is a consumer app that connects customers with restaurants and stores and delivers the order, usually in 10-40 minutes. It does not cook the food or (for now) own the groceries. It earns a **take rate**: commissions from restaurants and sellers, delivery and platform fees from customers, and advertising. The headline measure of activity is **gross order value (GOV)**, the total value of orders placed. Revenue is the slice of GOV that Swiggy keeps.

blocks.callout: **Why "adjusted" EBITDA?** Swiggy reports segment profit as adjusted EBITDA: it leaves out share-based pay (ESOP) and treats rent as an operating cost. Reported EBITDA does the reverse on rent (accounting rule Ind AS 116 moves it below EBITDA). In FY26 adjusted EBITDA was −₹2,871 cr and reported EBITDA −₹3,245 cr. The earnings-quality chapter walks through the bridge.

sections.title: Twelve years: from a Bengaluru food app to a cash-rich, loss-making platform

blocks.p: Swiggy started delivering food in Bengaluru in August 2014. It raised money privately for a decade, peaking at a US$10.7bn valuation in 2022 before investors marked it down to ~US$5.5bn in the 2023 tech downturn. It listed in November 2024 at ₹390. Since then it has raised ₹10,000 cr more through a QIP (Dec-2025, at ₹375), sold its stake in Rapido (₹2,399 cr) and agreed to sell a small distribution unit (Lynks). Each of these changed the numbers, as the table shows.

sections.title: Two markets, one dominant winner: Eternal

blocks.p: **Food delivery** in India is a two-player market: Eternal's Zomato and Swiggy. It became rational and profitable for both from 2023, once discount wars stopped. Zomato is bigger (its share of the two-player market has risen from ~54% in FY22 to ~57-58%), more profitable and growing faster. The market itself grows mid-to-high teens a year, helped by more users in smaller cities and more orders per user.

**Quick commerce** (groceries in 10-20 minutes) is the growth market: ~US$13-14bn of order value in FY26 and forecast at US$30bn by FY28 and US$50-57bn by FY30 (HSBC, Morgan Stanley). It is far more crowded: Blinkit (Eternal), Zepto, Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, BigBasket Now, Amazon Now and JioMart. Scale matters because a dark store is profitable only when it handles enough orders a day. Blinkit added 200 stores in Q1FY27 alone and guides to net order value growth "north of 60%" a year for three years.

sections.title: Food delivery: the engine, now earning ~3% of order value

blocks.p: Food delivery is Swiggy's profit engine. Order value rose from ₹28,784 cr in FY25 to ₹34,592 cr in FY26 (+20%) and adjusted EBITDA from ₹566 cr to ₹1,001 cr. In Q1FY27 GOV was ₹9,490 cr (+17.4%) and margin 3.1%, a seasonal dip from wage hikes and rider incentives. Contribution margin (profit after delivery and discounts, before fixed costs) is stable at ~7.6-7.8%, so the improvement comes from spreading fixed costs over more orders. Management guides to 18-20% GOV growth in FY27 and a 5% steady-state margin.

blocks.p: **Toing** is the wrinkle. It is a separate budget-meals app (~50 cities) that Swiggy reports under "platform innovations", not food. Platform innovations lost ₹131 cr in Q1FY27, almost half of food's profit, mostly on Toing marketing. Management argues it brings in new and lapsed users (two in three of its users); sceptics argue it cannibalises Swiggy's own food orders. By September, app data put Toing's weekly users (~33 mn) close to Zomato's (CLSA). We assume losses shrink from FY28 but do not assume it is closed.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** food delivery deserves a profit multiple, not a loss narrative. We forecast margin of 3.4% / 3.9% / 4.3% of GOV for FY27-29E (management's path is 5%; Zomato is already at 5.6%), giving adjusted EBITDA of {{F.seg.food.adjEbitda.0|num}} / {{F.seg.food.adjEbitda.1|num}} / {{F.seg.food.adjEbitda.2|num}} cr. The honest weakness: Swiggy is a permanent #2 with lower margins, and it is not winning share.

sections.title: Instamart: margins turning, losses deep, and a rival that has already won the scale race

blocks.p: Instamart delivers groceries and household items in ~10 minutes from 1,171 dark stores in 131 cities. Order value grew from ₹14,684 cr in FY25 to ₹28,496 cr in FY26, almost doubling, as Swiggy opened bigger stores and pushed into new cities. The cost was an adjusted EBITDA loss of ₹3,511 cr in FY26, more than three times what food delivery earned. In Q1FY27 order value was flat on the quarter (+40% on the year) as Swiggy cut unprofitable users, contribution margin reached breakeven in May, and the loss narrowed to ₹778 cr.

blocks.h: What has to happen for Instamart to break even

blocks.p: Management's own arithmetic (Q1 call and Capital Markets Day): Instamart needs ~₹60,000 cr of annualised net order value (about 2.5x today's ~₹23,268 cr) and a contribution margin of 5-6% (~₹30 per order) to break even at adjusted EBITDA. At ~30% growth that takes about three and a half years, so breakeven is roughly FY30, not FY28. For the next couple of quarters management guides contribution of 0 to −1% while growth accelerates (~75 new stores in Q2). The move to an inventory model should add ~80bp to contribution.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** we model losses of {{F.seg.im.adjEbitda.0|num}} / {{F.seg.im.adjEbitda.1|num}} / {{F.seg.im.adjEbitda.2|num}} cr for FY27-29E, i.e. still losing money in FY29. Revenue will jump in our forecast (Instamart revenue % of GOV rises from ~16% to ~55%) because the 1P model books the full sale value as revenue. That is an accounting change, not more profit. **Brutal truth:** Blinkit proves quick commerce can be profitable, but only for the leader. Instamart has half the stores, less than half the growth, and needs Blinkit to stay rational to reach breakeven.

sections.title: Out-of-home, supply chain and new bets: small, and mostly about costs

bullets: **Out-of-home (Dineout, events):** GOV ₹4,645 cr in FY26 and ₹1,529 cr in Q1FY27 (+45%), just profitable. Management targets scale and ~₹1,000 cr EBITDA by FY31. A genuine small positive; we value it at {{dcf.parts.2.value|num}} cr.

**Supply chain & distribution:** a low-margin wholesale business (₹10,935 cr revenue, −₹192 cr EBITDA in FY26) that sells to Instamart's sellers. It will shrink as Instamart buys stock directly and Lynks is sold (agreed Sep-2026). It matters for revenue, not value.

**Platform innovations (Toing, Pyng, Crew):** losses rose from ₹58 cr in Q4FY26 to ₹131 cr in Q1FY27 as Toing scaled. We deduct three years of FY28E losses ({{dcf.parts.4.value|num}} cr) from our valuation.

blocks.title: Moat scorecard vs Eternal
blocks.source: Swiggy and Eternal shareholder letters (Q1FY27), broker notes as cited, GAM Research

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Swiggy has a **durable position** in food delivery: it is one of only two national networks, with ~2.7 lakh restaurants, ~6.5 lakh delivery partners and a brand most urban Indians use. That position is hard to copy, which is why food earns money. But Swiggy has **no advantage over Eternal**, which is bigger, more profitable and growing faster in both food and quick commerce. In quick commerce, Swiggy has **no competitive advantage today**. Its strongest asset is its balance sheet, and cash is not a moat.

sections.title: Revenue is compounding; losses are not shrinking fast enough

blocks.p: Swiggy's revenue grew from ₹2,547 cr in FY21 to ₹23,053 cr in FY26, about 55% a year, and was up 37% year-on-year in Q1FY27 to ₹6,812 cr. But the company has never made an operating profit. The operating loss (EBITDA) was ₹3,235 cr in FY26 and the net loss ₹4,154 cr, larger than in FY24 or FY25, because the quick-commerce build-out (Instamart dark stores) is absorbing everything food delivery earns.

pair.title: Revenue: up 9x in five years
Net loss: bigger in FY26 than in FY24
The quarterly operating-loss margin is narrowing
…but absolute quarterly losses are still ~₹800 cr

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the margin trend is genuinely improving (EBITDA margin from −23% to −10% in three years), but because revenue is growing fast, the absolute loss has not fallen. Depreciation has doubled (₹612 cr in FY25 → ₹1,217 cr in FY26) as dark stores are added, so the path from EBITDA breakeven to net profit is longer still.

sections.title: Reported vs adjusted profit: the gap is ESOPs and rent

blocks.p: Swiggy's headline "adjusted EBITDA" is ₹374 cr better than reported EBITDA in FY26. Two items explain it. Share-based pay (₹966 cr) is excluded, which flatters adjusted EBITDA. Rent (₹607 cr) is included as a cost in adjusted EBITDA but moved below EBITDA in reported numbers, which flatters reported EBITDA. Neither number is the full picture: ESOPs are a real cost to shareholders (they are diluted), and rent is a real cash cost.

pair.title: FY26: from adjusted to reported EBITDA
ESOP cost is falling but still large

blocks.p: Two further accounting points: (1) Instamart's move to an inventory model will lift reported revenue sharply once it starts (within 2-4 quarters of the Aug-2026 approval) while cutting margins as a % of revenue; compare growth on order value, not revenue. (2) Instamart metrics are disclosed on both GOV and NOV (net of discounts) bases, and third-party reports mix them up; we use the company's letters throughout.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** No sign of aggressive accounting, but large ESOPs, adjusted metrics that exclude them, and a coming change in revenue recognition all make headline numbers harder to read.

sections.title: Cash burn: funded for now, but every quarter costs ~₹700 cr

blocks.p: Swiggy has burned operating cash every year: ₹2,898 cr in FY26 and ₹2,169 cr in FY25. Free cash flow (after capex) was −₹3,809 cr in FY26. The gap has been funded by equity: the November-2024 IPO (₹4,499 cr fresh) and the December-2025 QIP (₹10,000 cr at ₹375), plus the ₹2,399 cr sale of the Rapido stake. "Borrowings" of ~₹2,550 cr are almost entirely lease liabilities for dark stores and offices; there is no bank debt to speak of. Note that ~₹5,000 cr of bank deposits sit inside "other assets" on the balance sheet, so the company's own cash figure (₹15,053 cr at Mar-26) is higher than cash plus investments shown below.

The CFO expects to break even on cash over the next two quarters (excluding Toing). Our forecast has free cash flow of {{F.fcf.0|num}} / {{F.fcf.1|num}} / {{F.fcf.2|num}} cr in FY27-29E. In our bear case (Instamart losses stay near 10% of GOV) the cash pile keeps shrinking and another raise becomes likely by FY29.

sections.title: Ownership: foreign investors exiting, domestic funds absorbing

blocks.p: Swiggy has **no promoter**. The largest holders are Prosus (21.1%), SoftBank (6.3%) and the CEO (4.6%); Indian mutual funds own 22.77% and foreign portfolio investors 13.96% (Jun-2026). Two things are reshaping the register: **(1) the 49.5% foreign-ownership cap** (approved Aug-2026), which keeps Swiggy Indian-owned so it can hold Instamart inventory, but which led MSCI and NSE to drop the stock from foreign-investor indices in September; and **(2) the ₹10,000 cr QIP** (Dec-2025), over 80% bought by Indian investors.

sections.title: Our forecasts: losses narrow, but profit only arrives in FY29

blocks.p: We build the forecast business by business. Each segment's order value (or revenue) grows at our assumed rate; revenue and adjusted EBITDA are set as a % of it. Group reported EBITDA is the sum of the segments, less ESOP cost, plus rent (moved below EBITDA by accounting rules). Every assumption is listed, with our reasoning, in the Assumptions sheet of the Excel model, which recalculates this report's target price.

blocks.p: Most brokers stayed Buy after Q1 (Motilal Oswal, HDFC Securities, ICICI Securities, Nomura, Jefferies, Citi, UBS, JPMorgan, Bernstein, Nuvama) on the argument we share: food plus cash is worth about the market value, and Instamart is turning. CLSA, Morgan Stanley and HSBC are neutral; Macquarie (Underperform) and JM (Sell) worry about the burn. The median target is ₹360. Our food multiple (30x) is at the low end of the 30-40x range, and we give Instamart a small positive value (0.2x order value) where JM gives it zero.

sections.title: Valuation: sum of the parts, the street's method, gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}

blocks.p: Brokers value Swiggy **part by part (sum of the parts)**: food delivery on EV/EBITDA two years out (30-40x), Instamart on anything from zero to 0.5x net order value or a DCF, plus cash. ICICI Securities (and probably Emkay) use a whole-company DCF. We use the same method; P/E is meaningless while Swiggy loses money. The real debate is the food multiple and what Instamart is worth.

blocks.h: Sum of the parts in detail

blocks.p: A loss-making group of businesses cannot be valued on earnings. We value each business separately on our FY28E forecasts (sum of the parts), add the net cash we expect at March 2027, and deduct the cost of the new bets. Every input is live in the SOTP sheet of the Excel model, with Base / Bull / Bear switches.

bullets: **Food delivery:** Brokers value Swiggy food at 30-40x FY28E EBITDA (Anand Rathi 30x, MOFSL 32x, Elara 34x, JM 35x, Nomura and HDFC Sec 40x). Eternal's food business is valued at ~38x; 30x is a ~20% discount for lower margins and share loss.
**Instamart (quick commerce):** Blinkit is valued at ~1.2x GOV by brokers; Instamart at a deep discount as a distant #2. Adjustment = losses from FY28 until breakeven (bear: it never gets there).
**Supply chain & distribution:** Low-margin trading business shrinking as Instamart goes 1P.
**Platform innovations (Toing):** Capitalised cost of new bets: three years of FY28E losses (bull: shut in a year; bear: five years).
**Net cash at end-FY27E (after leases):** Model forecast: cash + investments + deposits − borrowings (incl. lease liabilities) at Mar-27.
**Add back lease liabilities:** Lease liabilities (₹2,451 cr, Mar-26) are dark-store rent obligations; segment EBITDA is after rent, so deducting them again would double count.

cells: Food margin rises to ~4.3% of GOV by FY29 and earns 30x; Instamart losses narrow from −9.8% of GOV but it still loses money in FY29; valued at 0.2x GOV less losses to come.

blocks.callout: **Cross-check: what is the market paying for?** Market value is ~₹69,031 cr. If food, out-of-home, supply chain, new bets and cash are worth what we think (₹72,500 cr), the market is valuing Instamart at about **−₹3,469 cr**. Put differently, with Instamart at zero, the price buys the food business at ~29x FY28E EBITDA, against ~42x that brokers apply to Zomato's food business. That gap is the upside case; Instamart's burn is the risk to it.

sections.title: Our honest summary: fairly priced for the food business; Instamart decides the rest

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a profitable, improving #2 food-delivery business plus ~₹14,367 cr of cash, at a price that gives quick commerce little value. Our target {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}) sits just short of our 15% BUY line.

**What can go wrong:** Instamart keeps losing ₹3,000 cr+ a year against a dominant, profitable Blinkit; growth targets keep being reset; food delivery keeps ceding share to Zomato; Toing keeps leaking cash; gig-worker levies and GST demands add costs. In that world the cash shrinks every quarter and the "food + cash" floor erodes. That is our bear case of {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

**Buy below ~₹250**, or if Instamart's quarterly loss falls below ₹600 cr while order value grows double digits on the quarter.
**Sell above ~₹300**, or if Instamart losses stay above ₹900 cr for two quarters, cash falls below ₹10,000 cr, or food growth drops below 15%.
**Position size if bought:** half a normal weight, built in tranches around results.

sections.title: Annotated financials
Glossary

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: Total value of orders placed by customers, including taxes, fees and tips, before discounts. The basic measure of how much business flows through the app.
Order value after all discounts. Instamart reports both; Blinkit reports NOV.
Revenue as a % of order value: the share Swiggy keeps through commissions, fees and advertising.
Profit on each order after delivery costs and discounts, before fixed costs such as technology and head office.
Swiggy's own profit measure: operating profit before ESOP cost, with rent treated as an operating cost.
Operating profit under accounting rules: includes ESOP cost, excludes rent (moved to depreciation and interest under Ind AS 116).
A small warehouse closed to the public, used only to pack quick-commerce orders.
The platform buys and owns the goods it sells (first party), booking the full sale value as revenue. The marketplace model only earns a fee on others' sales.
Indian-owned and controlled company. Only these may run an inventory e-commerce model; it requires foreign ownership below 50%.
Monthly transacting users: customers who ordered at least once in the month.
Employee stock options. A non-cash cost in the accounts, but it dilutes existing shareholders.
Qualified institutional placement: a share sale to institutional investors.
Sum of the parts: valuing each business separately and adding them up.
Enterprise value (market value less net cash) divided by EBITDA or by order value; used to value businesses that are not yet profitable.

assumptions._note: Segment-driven model: each business's driver (GOV or revenue) grows; revenue and adjusted EBITDA are % of the driver. Consolidated reported EBITDA = sum of segment adjusted EBITDA − ESOP + Ind AS 116 rent add-back. Valued on sum of the parts (FY28E). ₹ crore.

segments.name: Food delivery
segments._why: Q1FY27 GOV +17.4% (~18% excluding LPG-led restaurant cancellations); management guides 18-20% (ex-Toing) for FY27. We stay at the low end because Zomato is growing faster (NOV +20.1% in Q1).
segments._revWhy: Take rate (commission + fees + ads) 23.3% of GOV in H1FY27, up from 22.6% in FY26.
segments._marginWhy: 2.9% in FY26, 3.1% in Q1FY27 (a seasonal dip from wage hikes and delivery-partner spend). Management's steady-state target is 5%; Zomato already earns 5.6% of NOV. We assume ~0.45pp a year.

segments.name: Instamart (quick commerce)
segments._why: Q1FY27 GOV +39.8% YoY but flat on Q4FY26; management is "cautiously optimistic" of at least double-digit sequential growth from Q2. Double-digit QoQ growth for Q2-Q4 gives FY27 ~+30%. Blinkit grows ~86%, so we fade growth.
segments._revWhy: Revenue is ~15.6% of GOV (Q1FY27) under the marketplace model. Shareholders approved the 49.5% foreign cap (18-Aug-2026), so Instamart can own inventory (1P) within 2-4 quarters; 1P books the full sale value as revenue.
segments._marginWhy: Adjusted EBITDA −9.8% of GOV in Q1FY27 (contribution margin −0.2%, breakeven in May-2026). Management guides contribution margin of 0 to −1% for the next couple of quarters while growth accelerates, and EBITDA breakeven only at ~2.5x today's scale. We assume −9.2% / −5% / −2%.

segments.name: Out-of-home (Dineout, events)
segments._why: Q1FY27 GOV +44.8%. FY31 target >₹10,000 cr adjusted EBITDA for the group includes out-of-home scale-up.
segments._marginWhy: 0.6% in FY26, 0.7% in H1FY27; target 4%+ by FY31.

segments.name: Supply chain & distribution
segments._why: This unit sells goods to Instamart's sellers. When Instamart buys inventory itself (1P), most of this revenue moves inside Instamart, so it shrinks. Lynks (a distribution unit) was sold in Q2FY27.
segments._marginWhy: −1.8% in FY26; Lynks sale adds ~₹20 cr a quarter from Q3FY27.

segments.name: Platform innovations (Toing, new bets)
segments._why: Toing (affordable meals app, ~50 cities) is scaling: adjusted revenue ₹69 cr in Q1FY27, +156% YoY.
segments._marginWhy: Adjusted EBITDA −₹131 cr in Q1FY27 (−190% of adjusted revenue), mostly Toing user-acquisition marketing. We assume the loss ratio halves each year as Toing scales or is reined in.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Ind AS 116 rent add-back (negative = raises reported EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Segment adjusted EBITDA is after dark-store and office rent; reported EBITDA moves rent below EBITDA (into depreciation and interest). FY26 ₹607 cr; Q2FY27 ₹184 cr a quarter and rising with stores.
assumptions._esopWhy: Share-based pay: ₹1,173 cr FY25, ₹966 cr FY26, ₹367 cr in H1FY27. Non-cash, but it dilutes shareholders.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex (~₹700 cr, management says it falls in FY27) plus the principal part of lease payments (~₹550 cr), because reported EBITDA excludes rent.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Other income ₹504 cr in FY26 on average cash of ~₹11,000 cr; ₹423 cr in H1FY27.
assumptions._taxWhy: Losses: no tax until accumulated losses are used up.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: Swiggy is five businesses at very different stages (profitable food, loss-making Instamart): each needs its own yardstick. Primary method.

methods.name: EV/GOV
methods.why: How the market compares delivery platforms that do not yet make profits. Eternal trades at ~2x its order value; Swiggy at ~0.5x FY26 GOV today. 0.6x FY28E GOV is a ~70% discount to Eternal for lower margins and share loss.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Food margins reach ~5% by FY29 and earn 38x; Instamart grows faster, loses less and is valued at 0.5x GOV; Toing is shut.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Food keeps losing share (22x on lower margins); Instamart growth slows and losses stay high, so quick commerce is worth less than nothing; Toing keeps burning.

assumptions._depWhy: FY26 actual ~20% on a smaller, younger block; H1FY27 run-rate ~₹1,210 cr a year ≈ 16% of gross block.
